text:
Before you hire someone for a task, do it yourself for a week and write down every step.

If you cannot write the steps down, a new hire cannot follow them, and neither can software.

You do not have to feel like following up.

Open the message, type two lines and send it, because the customer cannot tell what mood you were in.

Your customers will never see the week you almost closed the business.

They only see whether you picked up the phone.

Tell your client the bad news in the same hour you find it.

They can plan around a problem, but they cannot plan around silence.

Saying your price out loud feels heavy only until you hear the answer.

Say the number, stop talking and let the customer reply, because filling the silence is how discounts begin.

At the end of the week, count the invoices you sent and the quotes you chased, not the hours you felt busy.

Busy is a feeling, but a sent invoice is something your bank account can see.

You do not need a website to sell your first service.

Message the people who already know your work, tell them what you now offer and what it costs, and let their answers shape everything else.

Let AI write the first draft of your customer emails, but never let it send one.

The draft saves you time, and the minute you spend reading it is what keeps your name safe.

Charge a deposit before you start any job, even for customers you like.

A deposit shows you who is serious, and it means a cancelled job still covers the time you held for it.
